Question: Is Dry Shampoo safe?
Answer: Dry shampoo is not the panacea it used to be when the first commercially produced dry shampoo was sold in the 1940s. Image from Unsplash - Kalos Skincare Besides a cancer scare over Unilever products, many hair care experts worry about dry shampoo's impact on the scalp. At the end of 2022, approximately 19 dry shampoos were recalled due to a potential cancer risk. Dry shampoo products manufactured by Unilever were found to contain potentially dangerous benzene levels, suspected to be a human carcinogen. When the elevated levels were discovered, they triggered a recall, and the FDA was concerned. Brands including Dove, Nexxus, Suave, Tresemme, and Bed Head were recalled. Some hair experts are against dry shampoo because of potential damage to the scalp. One outspoken expert who specializes in scalp restoration is Lars Skjoth. He is the chief inventor behind the Harlinikken hair care line, which promotes healthy hair regrowth. In October 1992, at the age of 25, he opened his first Harklinikkin clinic in Copenhagen. He said in an interview with Mr.Feelgood magazine, "I'm probably one of the most unpopular people in the hair industry in one area, in the way that I am very much against dry shampoo, for example, that has absolutely nothing to do with shampoo." He pointed out: "It just gives you the illusion of recently shampooed hair, but it can cause a lot of irritation to the scalp and things like that." Specializing in treating, nurturing, and guiding new and healthier growth According to an interview in Mr.Feelgood magazine, Lars' raison d’être and expertise "is grounded in identifying and arresting scalp and hair degeneration at any age." He specializes in "treating, nurturing, and guiding new and healthier growth." Lars Skjoth knows what he's talking about regarding cleaning products. If he is against dry shampoo, there is a good reason. Other experts believe dry shampoo should only be used in emergencies and never two days in a row. Question: I'm only 20 and I'm already fed up with humanity. How can I live with this species for the rest of my life?
Answer: I used to work for Gary, the CEO of a high-tech start-up company. One day, he told me a story I’ve never forgotten, even 24 years later. Gary told me that his father would take him to a giant Easter Egg Hunt at a large private country club, every year. It was always swarming with kids. Some of the eggs hidden around the huge club had cash or tickets for fabulous prizes. The stakes were high for all the children. The first year, Gary ran out the gate and followed the crowd. There was a lot of punching, kicking, pinching and shoving. Gary had to fight tooth and nail to snag a few eggs. Run In The Opposite Direction After the hunt, his father sat him down. He told Gary, “Next year, if all the kids run to the right, you should run in the opposite direction. Ditch the crowd and hunt for yourself.” Gary followed his dad's advice. He found the most eggs, won the most cash, and received some great prizes every following year. How does Gary's egg story relate to being fed up humanity? More importantly, how can you live with the human race/species for the rest of your life? Run The Opposite Direction From Humanity - At Least Temporarily Consider following Gary’s philosophy. But plan to distance yourself from any and all people who are stressing you out. At least for the short-term. Give yourself a break to help you reboot your attitude. It’s amazing what a little time out can do for everyone. Sometimes we need to get away from annoying people, places and events they populate. Structure your life to minimize unnecessary interactions. Give yourself a much-needed break from humanity in any way you can. Rearrange Your Travel Times And Routes If traffic or other drivers bothers you, arrange to travel when less people are on the roads. Experiment with traveling earlier than normal. When you arrive early use the extra time to relax, read a book, meditate, or even take a quick cat nap. Or take the least traveled roads to avoid crowds and people. Adopt New Coping Skills Not everyone has the option to avoid annoying people. But if if you can, experiment with adopting new habits to help you cope. Work on your perspective. Commit to spending special time nourishing yourself. Get more rest and sleep, eat healthy foods, exercise, take a relaxing walk or meditate. Treat yourself with special kindness and self-love. It’s easier to be accepting and compassionate to other people if you treat yourself well. Would A Therapist Be Helpful? If life adjustments don’t help your frustrations, consider talking to a therapist. Or a trusted friend or family member. Are your feelings temporary, or are they a symptom of something deeper? Maybe humanity stressing you out is a side issue. Do you have other deeper and trauma related issues that are triggering you? Sometimes the Universe is a mirror. Other people annoy us because of other inner challenges requiring attention. One way to learn to live with annoying people is to practice gratitude. Try making a gratitude list in the morning when you first wake up and right before you go to sleep at night. If you can focus on the good things in your life, it may be easier to tolerate people who frustrate or annoy you. Consider practicing random acts of kindness. It’s amazing how wonderful life can feel when you are being kind so someone else. It will may lift your own frustrations about dealing with annoying people. There Are Many Options To Consider There are many ways you can structure your life according to your own needs. The requirements to live with humanity for the rest of your life doesn't have to be a death sentence. The good news? You’re starting early at age 20. You can structure your life so that you can peacefully and happily exist with other humans.

Question: Can you make money on Medium?
Answer: Yes, you can make money on Medium, and some people do, but based upon my personal experience, Medium is highly political. It’s also huge, chaotic and seems to take sudden shifts without warning? Does it support writers? Hmmm. Maybe not so much anymore. One thing seems true based on my own experience, if you’re in the publication power circles, you can do even better than if you’re not. AI Dangers Are Dawning on Medium One of the most respected writers on Medium is Linda Carroll. She writes a Substack newsletter and is definitely worth following if you’re interested in writing on Medium. Even more so if you’re interested in making money writing on that platform. In her newsletter dated 4/12/24 the always wise writer addresses the new Medium AI policy which says, “Beginning May 1, 2024, stories with AI-generated writing (disclosed as such or not) are not allowed to be paywalled.” Ms. Carroll notes: “It’s the “disclosed or not” part that concerns me.” She explains: ”Last May I wrote about freelance writers who are having pay withheld or getting fired for using AI—when they didn’t. AI detection tools suck. Open AI created ChatGPT but their own AI detection can’t tell AI content from content written by humans.” Can You Get Fired From Medium? Ms. Carroll makes a very important point about writers getting fired from Medium. It’s happening with increasingly frequency and regular writer purges occur. Yes, in some cases there are scammers and other bad seeds, but good, hard working writers may get accidentally caught up in a purge. Even if you never use AI tools of any kind, you may still land on the wrong side of the Medium police. . And yes the Customer Care people at Medium are famous for missing a kindness or compassion chip for writers. As Ms. Carroll reported, “In late March, Medium banned a bunch of accounts for fraudulent activity. There’s a ton of fraud on Medium. People impersonating writers, people setting up multiple accounts to inflate earnings, inauthentic engagement like people clapping and commenting on posts they haven’t read to inflate engagement stats. So they whacked a bunch. 1.7% of Medium accounts in one fell swoop. Which doesn’t sound like much until you do the math. Medium has over a million paid members. Roughly 17K accounts were suspended. Poof. Done.” Unfortunately there were innocent writers who got caught up in the traps and were swept out by mistake. Medium reinstated some, but not all of the accounts who claimed to be innocent of any wrongdoing. But those who weren’t guilty and didn’t get reinstated? They’re out, permanently. Yes and, here is the super scary part about Medium: Can you be capriciously banned from Medium? Yes you can. Just ask formed Medium writer David Perlmutter from Canada who writers on Substack. Christopher Lancett, another formed Medium writer wrote in a February 3, 2022 post, “Medium, as a quick aside, deserves to be driven out of business because of its increasingly writer-hostile changes.” One Strike And You’re Out - Forever Think about it, even criminals get three strikes before they’re out. They get a trial and are presumed innocent until proven guilty. Of course Medium is a privately owned platform and they can remove any writers they want whenever they want for any reason they deem is appropriate. Even if its all rotten baloney. The same is true of other Social Media platforms like X or LinkedIn or Facebook, although many platforms provide warnings, are open to redemption and good faith amends. Many provide a system of at least three strikes before permanent death. And by the way, if you are targeted, it doesn’t matter if you pay the higher Friend of Medium monthly fees, it doesn’t matter if you’ve spent hundreds of hours volunteering as an editor or publisher. Nope. If they decide you’re out, you’re out. End of the story. How scary is that? Medium Celebrity Writers Yes, you can make money, but there are many secrets and games you have to play to make significant amounts. Those secrets and games can be learned but beware of being too successful. Some celebrity writers who have been on the platform a long time and built many thousands of followers, understand their niche and write every day can do very well. But they are the exception to the rule. Medium requires that you play a long game, work hard, write as well as you can, and be consistent. It may take years to build enough followers and engagement to make more than a a little money every month. Competition Is Fierce Linda Carroll, in her April 5th newsletter shared the following statistics about Medium: “In 2018, Medium was publishing 20,000 stories per day. 591,000/month. In 2020, Medium was publishing 47,000 stories per day. 1,385,000/month. In 2024, Medium publishes 82,759 stories per day. 2.4 million in February.” Think about shouting into the abyss. Now think about shouting into Medium. Plus, shadow banning is very common. So even if you get your voice out there, Medium may shut it down. Your voice is competing with 2.4 million other stories (articles in Medium-speak) or more every month on Medium. That’s a lot of other writers to compete with on a platform that has shown a lack of empathy, compassion and understanding to writers who are paying them a monthly fee to be on their platform. Can you make money on Medium? Yes, of course. But what is your definition of money? Is it $1.00 a month or maybe $1,000 a month? Even some of the top Medium writers have been reporting a major downturn in their earnings, especially since Medium introduced their new Boost program in 2023. For some people Medium is the best platform for their writing goals. But it may prove challenging for many. Be sure to do extensive research before you jump into the Medium writing pool to make sure you truly understand the platform’s environment.

Question: What happens to you when your long-time therapist dies?
Answer: I first met Betty Alice Erickson in August of 1992 when my husband went to see her to prepare for major heart therapy. She smiled warmly, extended her hand (pre-Covid) and introduced herself to me as I sat nervously in the waiting the room. Besides being the daughter of the famed Dr. Milton Erickson who was known as The Father of Hypnotherapy, she was a renowned therapist in her own right. Image of Dr. Milton Erickson on Wikipedia - Creative Commons Her expertise was hypnotherapy which she learned from her father. Teaching My Husband And I Hypnotherapy Over the next four weeks Betty, as she preferred to be called, taught my husband to hypnotize himself so he could get through open heart surgery with the least amount of trauma. His treatment was a rousing success. Not only did he require less anesthesia, he woke up quickly from the surgery, much to the surprise of his surgeons. During his post-surgical visits to Betty to deal with the grief he experienced from his major surgery on his heart, she approached me after one of his visits. The Beginning Of Our Longtime Journey She handed me her card and said, “Call me anytime. I can see you’re probably suffering from PTSD from all that your husband has been through for the past year.” I burst into tears right ten and there. She leaned over and gave me a warm hug and I was grateful for her compassion. Shorty after that breakthrough in her office, I made my first appointment with Betty. A 21 Year Long On/Off Relationship Over the years I continued to see her on and off until 2014 right before her death from throat cancer in January of 2015. Even thought I new it was coming, when she died I was set adrift in a sea of shock, deep sadness and grief. When I say on/off, I mean that we would work on one of my key issues during a few sessions. She would always give me homework in-between sessions, which I would faithfully complete before our next time together. Once I completed a journey to understand, heal and release one major life trauma or issue, she would temporarily fire me. She would tell me to just take some time to love myself. I could always come back when I was ready to do more work. And I did go back. Over and over for many years. Then I Couldn’t Go Back Again Until I couldn’t go back anymore, because she was gone. Betty Erickson helped me to heal a lifetime of physical, mental, emotional and verbal abuse. She also was the keeper of all my secrets. She knew more about me than anyone else in the Universe. All the personal information I’d shared with another living being vanished forever. What happens to you when your long-time therapist dies? In my case I mourned Betty’s passing for a year. Then I tried to find another therapist. Unfortunately, or fortunately, depending on your perspective, the first three told me they couldn’t help me with anything. What? Did that mean I was on the verge of total mental meltdown? No, it meant that I had spent the last 21 years walking into my most traumatic life experiences headfirst and battling the demons until they surrended. Betty had helped me fine tune self-compassion, understanding, wisdom and self-forgiveness. I eventually found a much older therapist with over 25 years of experience who could pick up and help me where Betty left off. What happen to you when your therapist dies? It depends on a wide range of variables depending upon how many years you worked with the therapist (history means a lot) and the seriousness of the issues you’ve been addressing. Should you get another therapist? It’s not like buying another plant when one dies. It’s all dependent on the individual, their needs and the relationship they had in the past. xo

Question: What is something shocking to you about Albert Einstein's life?
Answer: While he was alive, my late husband, a tested and documented math genius, often referenced how much his life was very similar to that of Albert Einstein. Portrait of Einstein taken in 1935 at Princeton - Wikipedia Yes, he had lots of thick, curly hair, which seemed to sprout all over his head like he just stuck his finger in a light socket. He was always disheveled, often cut the buttons off his jackets and shirts, and was very forgetful, even when he could be a genius with math and science. Like Einstein, he loved to doodle math equations on every imaginable surface he could find if he didn’t have paper and pencil nearby. I’d find his math equations written on the surface of his wooden desk or on the side of the wall next to his desk. My late husband had a lot of similar likes and lifestyle preferences like Einstein. It was uncanny. Whenever he would tell me “Einstein” used to do this, I would go look it up, and sure enough. he was always right, and it was uncanny. Sometimes, I would tease him about it, but mostly, I would be amazed. Other people might mention similarities, and I would be surprised. My late husband graduated from Harvard with a degree in math, but he took classes at Princeton. In fact, he was taking classes in math or science until his untimely death. He studied his entire life. I used to laugh about all the similarities until the last Einstein similarity was tragic, shocking me to my core. Einstein passed away in 1955. My husband died in 2005. I have no explanation for why my husband had so many similarities to Einstein, but when he died exactly the same way that Einstein did, I was angry with myself for not knowing that and maybe trying to figure out a way to prevent it from happening to my husband. Of course, it was just a coincidence, but it still shocked me when it happened. Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm My late husband, who passed away suddenly in April of 2005, died from a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. In his youth, he smoked but gave it up in his 40s. He spoke fluent German, Russian, and Spanish and spent 4 years living in Germany and Europe. He was also a vegetarian during the last years of his life. Einstein had a respect for vegetarianism and may have dabbled with it himself. Ironically, Einstein died of a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm on April 18, 1955. He was 76. Einstein was a devotee of pipe smoking. Smoking makes one roughly eight times more likely to develop an aneurysm. Many things shocked me about Albert Einstein’s life, but his death shocked me the most of all when I researched it after my own husband died the exact same way.

Question: Why does my 3b/c low porosity (I think) hair feels dry and brittle. (1/2)?
Answer: Unfortunately, over the years, much content has been written about knowing your exact hair characteristic numbers. So much so that some people develop anxiety about it. Maybe I’m getting older, or maybe I’ve just been hanging around in the hair industry for way too many years, but in my personal experience, I have discovered that while it’s helpful to have a good idea about your hair type, it’s not all that important if you have 3 b/c low porosity versus 1/2. What is important is that your hair is feeling dry and brittle, which means something is not working well for you. Flat Cuticles Don’t Easily Allow Moisture Into The Cuticle With low-porosity hair, the difficulty lies in getting moisture into the hair. The cuticle tends to lay flat, which blocks moisture from getting in. Once you get it in, the good news is that the cuticle will lock it in. The key is getting the right amount of moisture into your hair in the first place.z If your hair isn’t getting the moisture it needs, it will react by becoming dry, crunchy, and brittle. It will make it more prone to breakage. Heat Is The Answer To Low Porosity Hair Heat opens the cuticle. You don’t want to go with extreme heat, which can be damaging, so you have a few options: Use Cold Air To Dry Hair Remember that heat opens the cuticle and will allow all the moisture you just packed in with the deep or leave-in conditioners to escape. If you must air dry, only use cold air. It may not feel as nice, but you want to keep the cuticle flat. Use A Hood Dryer, Blow Dryer, Or Heat Cap For Deep Conditioning Not everyone likes deep conditioning in the shower. You can also use a hairdryer to open your cuticle and apply deep conditioner. Get hair doused with lukewarm water. Accordion squeeze to remove water. Slather on a deep conditioner, sit under a hood dryer or use a blow dryer set on warm or a heat cap to push the conditioner deep down into your cuticle. Minimize Use Of Hair Chemicals Avoid using chemicals as much as possible on your hair. Chemicals such as hair color, straighteners, relaxers, or perms will lift the cuticle, allowing moisture to escape. Hair becomes dry, crunchy, and brittle. Bleach will also lift the cuticle, which is why some bleached hair is so dry and brittle. Skip The Hair Oils Any type of hair oil may block moisture from entering or leaving the hair. Oil creates a barrier around the hair strands, preventing much-needed moisture from getting into the cuticles. Low-porosity hair has high moisture retention once you get moisture into the hair. You don’t want to use oils because this often makes low-porosity hair feel dry and crunchy. Keep Scalp And Hair Free Of Product Buildup Make sure to wet wash your scalp and hair regularly to remove any product build-up. Not All Hydrating Products Work For All People Unfortunately, this is an ongoing challenge of mine. When I find a product for my hair that works wonders, the manufacturers habitually change the formulas or substitute ingredients. Find products that promise to result in high levels of hydration. Then, use heat to get the moisture into your cuticle and cold to lock it in. Minimize the use of chemicals and baby your hair. All of these suggestions can help. Find a hair expert who understands your hair type, texture, and unique requirements and ask for their input on products that might work best for your type of porosity. Like anything else, your hair is an ongoing learning experience. Best wishes.

Question: What did Elon Musk's recently released biography by Walter Isaacson reveal about Amber Heard?
Answer: The new biography of Elon Musk by Walter Isaacson says: Most of Musk’s relationships involve psychological turmoil. 'The most agonizing of them all was with the actress Amber Heard, who drew him into a dark vortex that lasted more than a year and produced deep-seated pain that lingers today. 'It was brutal', Isaason wrote. Elon Musk’s friends ‘hated’ Amber Heard. Musk tends to be a “fool for love.” Elon Musk’s brother and friends “hated” actor Amber Heard while the pair were dating. “Musk was not bred for domestic tranquility,” Isaacson writes, adding that most of his relationships “involve psychological turmoil.” According to the biography, “The most agonizing” of Musk’s affairs was his romance with Amber Heard, amid her divorce from Johnny Depp.” Musk says of their year-long relationship from January to December 2017 that it was truly brutal. They broke up for a brief period in July. Then Heard and Musk would continue dating for another “tumultuous five months,” Isaacson writes. Their relationship ended during a “wild trip” to Rio de Janeiro, when Heard allegedly locked herself in their room and became paranoid she would be attacked and that “Elon had taken her passport.” The Aquaman actor, who was also interviewed for the biography, admits she “got rather dramatic” during the argument in Brazil but tells Isaacson they made up afterward. At one point, Musk’s chief-of-staff Sam Teller compares Heard to the Joker in Batman. Musk’s brother Kimbal highlights: “The way she can create her own reality reminds me of my dad.” Another one of Musk’s former partners, Grimes (real name Claire Boucher), said Musk is attracted to “chaotic evil” while discussing his relationship with Heard. “My Dungeons & Dragons alignment would be chaotic good. Whereas Amber’s is probably chaotic evil,” she explained, referring to her and Musk’s shared love for the fantasy game. “He’s attracted to chaotic evil. It’s about his father [Errol] and what he grew up with, and he is quick to fall back into being treated badly. He associates love with being mean or abusive. There’s an Errol-Amber through line. A small but significant piece of the book offers a window into his relationship with Amber Heard, the actor who, at this point, is best known for enduring a painfully public defamation lawsuit with her ex-husband, Johnny Depp. Regarding Musk, though, the Heard portion of Isaacson’s book shows a man who is ultimately and impossibly human despite his comfort with rockets and robots, the singularity, and the simulation. The time Musk spent involved with Heard made for a short chapter in his life but an impactful one, to say the least. According to the book, they first met because, in 2012, she was preparing for her role in Machete Kills, which involved a character trying to create a society on a space station. He was tapped as a consultant, but they didn’t connect until a year later. She toured SpaceX, and he drove her around in a Tesla. They reconnected when her marriage with Depp was circling the drain. Heard and Musk reacquainted themselves at the Met Gala in 2016. They saw each other while waiting to walk the red carpet. Within the month, Heard filed for the now-infamous divorce from Depp. Their early dates apparently revolved around his work. Musk flew Heard and her sister to see the Falcon 9 launch at Cape Canaveral, and she flew from Italy to the Fremont Tesla factory for his birthday that June. Isaacson describes how Heard picked wildflowers on the way and hid in the back of a Tesla to surprise him. In April 2017, he joined her in Australia, where she was filming Aquaman. The tabloid media caught on at that time after they shared photos at dinner together. Per Isaacson, they still enjoyed dates at a rope course and wildlife sanctuary, everyman excursions. Less typically, “He told her that she reminded him of Mercy, his favorite character in the video game Overwatch, so she spent two months designing and commissioning a head-to-toe costume to role-play for him,” Isaacson wrote. As romantic and specific to them as all of this sounds, all parties involved, including Heard and Musk, admit that the relationship was not always smooth. Musk’s brother, Kimbal Musk, called Heard “toxic” and “a nightmare.” He said she reminded him of his dad, one of the worst things a Musk brother could say about someone. (Errol Musk and his estrangement from Elon makes for a significant portion of Isaacson’s book.) Musk’s chief of staff compared Heard to “the Joker” and said that she “thrives on destabilizing everything.” (Vanity Fair has attempted to reach out to Heard.) When they broke up in the summer of 2017, Musk entered into a period that Isaacson calls “the most hellacious period of his life” emotionally and professionally. (Besides the breakup with Heard, Musk had also learned his father, Errol, fathered a child with his stepdaughter, Jana, whom Errol had raised from childhood.) Musk calls it the most “concentrated pain” he’d ever felt and “eighteen months of unrelenting insanity” that was “mind-bogglingly painful.” Heard spoke to Isaacson for the book too, especially regarding one of their last trips together that involved a big fight where she became paranoid that her passport was taken from her. Heard confirmed that they argued that night but that they made up too. “I love him very much,” she told the author. “Elon loves fire, and sometimes it burns him.”

Question: What is the real reason Rory Gilmore didn't go to Harvard and went to Yale instead?
Answer: The Gilmore Girls costume designer addressed rumors that Rory didn't attend Harvard over filming restrictions. Fans of the show have been taken along for the ride as Rory (Alexis Bledel) starts out as a teenage bookworm trying to realize her dream of getting into Harvard University. But the big twist came in season three in 2003, when Rory ultimately decided to go to rival school Yale instead. Rumors have circulated for years that the reason for Rory's shocking college choice was due to alleged filming regulations at the different Ivy Leagues, with show creator Amy Sherman-Palladino telling Deseret News in 2002 that Yale would "let us film there, which makes it a lot easier." But now, Gilmore Girls costumer Valerie Campbell setting the record straight, saying that wasn't really the full picture. Responding to a TikTok user who wrote, "I thought it was because Yale agreed to let them film there and Harvard did not," Valerie noted in a September 5 video that the crew could have made either school work because they actually shot at "fake" Harvard and "fake" Yale across multiple episodes. "What they did not take into consideration was we didn't shoot at Harvard, but we also didn't shoot at Yale," the costumer explained. "That is not the reason why we didn't shoot at Harvard. We would have if we wanted to build Harvard on a stage." Indeed, scenes from Rory and mom Lorelai(Lauren Graham) traveling to Harvard's Massachusetts campus were actually filmed at UCLA in Los Angeles, whereas her first visit to Yale's Connecticut campus was shot at Pomona College in Claremont, Calif., according to Yale Alumni Magazine. The crew member said she didn't remember "any conversations" about the crew being unable to film at the real Crimson grounds. So, a year ago, she reached out to an unnamed writer on the show for clarity. The scriptwriter also didn't know why they switched, but "didn't think" it was related to Harvard, recalled Valerie, who was also a costume supervisor on Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life. Instead, it may have had to do with the Gilmore family feud involving Rory's grandparents Emily (Kelly Bishop) and Richard (Edward Herrmann). "My guess is that we thought it made for [an] interesting story," Valerie remembered hearing. "Rory and Lorelai had this plan for years, and then just when it's about to become a reality, Rory essentially chooses Richard and Emily's side by picking Yale." Ultimately, the Gilmore Girls team built sets in Burbank, Calif., to look like Yale's campus, which Valerie noted was closer to Rory's fictional home in Stars Hollow, Conn. to allow more onscreen interactions with her family. At the time, production designer Lauren Crasco explained why they chose Rory's specific dorm, telling Yale Alumni Magazine in 2003, "Calhoun was easiest to replicate. Plus, it has these high wood panels and stone arches that play great on film." They ultimately used a material similar to bulletin boards to build walls, with crushed walnut shells for additional texture, according to the outlet. "Rory's crucial visit was actually filmed at Pomona College, and despite the crew's best efforts to avoid shots with palm trees, the classic Southern California architecture looked absurdly unlike New England," reporter Michael Taylor wrote at the time. "But with Rory slated to be a full-time student, it made fiscal sense to build a more authentic slice of Yale."

Question: What is the ongoing controversy around the podcast My Favorite Murder?
Answer: My Favorite Murder True Crime Podcasters Have A Growing List Of Controversies The true crime genre has raised a bevy of concerns over how ethical it is to profit and obsess over real-life crimes and victims, which makes the many controversies of My Favorite Murder quite relevant to this conversation. The podcast My Favorite Murder joined the true crime craze in 2016 and has since become one of the highest-grossing podcasts of all time, making its hosts, Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark, multi-millionaires. Image from Unsplash On top of the millions they already earned, Kilgariff and Hardstark recently signed a $100 million deal with Amazon, which has its share of controversies. True crime has become controversial in some circles primarily due to a perceived lack of empathy from some other true crime authors and followers, who go as far as to call themselves “fans” of true crime. The winds of true crime have been changing over the past few years, with some true crime writers and podcasters focusing more on the victims and also turning up their empathy chip for the families and other potential victims. My Favorite Murder takes on an even more problematic premise than most true crime works, though, as it claims to be a “true crime comedy.” A Rise In Distaste For True Crime Comedy Taking a step past the rising concerns for lack of victim empathy, criticism has been leveled against My Favorite Murder for weaving comedy into the tragic lives of real-life crime victims. As a long-term True Crime writer, I have always been extremely sensitive to the needs of the victims and their families when I pick which cases to highlight. While many true crime podcasts like Vigilante, The Retrievals, and Scamanda are hosted by veteran journalists, true crime writers, or licensed private investigators, My Favorite Murder features two hosts with backgrounds in comedy. There really is no place for comedy in the world of true crime. I also believe that My Favorite Murder has given the True Crime genre a bad name in some cases. Others agree with me. The podcast tackles true crime through a humorous and gossipy lens, which isn’t always the most sensitive or factual. Unsurprisingly, their problematic approach to true crime and insensitivity has stirred up several controversies. My Own Experience Dealing With True Crime Writing in 2023 When I wrote my first True Crime Book, which was published in June of 2023 - How To Avoid Murder While Using Dating Apps - I was very concerned with each and every victim in the 8 stories that are featured in my book. How one can be a fan of gruesome and tragic cases that impacted real-life victims is unclear. However, the genre has led to many problems, including insensitivity towards victims, spotlighting atrocious criminals, and spurning netizens to become problematic internet sleuths and interfere in open cases. My Favorite Murder insensitivity and ignorance Other significant controversies surrounding My Favorite Murder have resulted from insensitivity and ignorance by its hosts. This isn’t very surprising considering that the entire premise of My Favorite Murder is insensitive and run by two hosts who former fans have accused of becoming increasingly resistant to criticism, feedback, and change. As a result, Kilgariff and Hardstark have ventured into some pretty offensive territory in the past. One prime example of their insensitivity and ignorance dates back to 2017 when they released a T-shirt for their podcast with a tipi printed on its front. The Uproar Over The Tipi A tipi is seen by many as indigenous cultural appropriation. This symbol bumps up against the skyrocketing rates for Indigenous women living on reservations which is 10 times the national average. Their use of the tipi (/ˈtiːpiː/"TEE-pee"), often called a lodge in English, is a conical tent, historically made of animal hides or pelts, and in more recent generations of canvas, stretched on a framework of wooden poles. The Murder Of Indigenous Women However, when studies have found that murder rates for Indigenous women living on reservations are 10 times higher than the national average, such a flippant and thoughtless quote alongside a tipi is inexcusable. Hardstark and Kilgariff vaguely addressed and apologized for the situation. Have Negative Comments On Instagram Been Deleted? However, Hardstark was accused of deleting comments about the situation on the podcast's Instagram and even liking a racist comment defending the t-shirt. Later, she apologized for liking the comment, and she and Kilgariff donated to the First Nations Development Institute. Did Kilgariff & Hardstark Wait Too Long To Stop Selling The T-Shirts With The Tipi According to some TikTok users, Kilgariff and Hardstark took what many considered a very long time to take down the merch from their website, likely selling plenty before finally removing them as promised. It's unclear how much Hardstark learned about sensitivity from the aforementioned incident, considering that she posted another extremely offensive and triggering post on social media in 2019. Anatomical Dolls For Child Sex Abuse Cases - Crying With Glee In the post, Hardstark was raving about and posing with anatomical dolls used in cases of child sex abuse. She even wrote that she was "a sick, sick person" for almost "crying with glee" over the dolls. Of course, this was highly triggering to many, especially abuse survivors, and simply incomprehensible to anyone why she would post this. The T-Shirt Controversy Hardstark’s response to the backlash was eerily similar to the t-shirt controversy and included an apology and donation to a charity advocating against child abuse. However, that incident should’ve proven that her insensitivity had gone too far and that maybe her career shouldn’t be based on discussing true crime. Problematic Framing of Crime and Law Enforcement Another major problem with My Favorite Murder is how it handles crime, law enforcement, and criminal justice. The podcast largely ignores Black, Indigenous, and women of color (BIPOC) cases and focuses primarily on cases only involving white women. This is disappointing and problematic because it creates the illusion that white women are the most common victims of true crime. It also exaggerates the likelihood of anyone being a victim of a serious crime like homicide. Romanticizing Law Enforcement To diffuse the unfounded fears they raise, Kilgariff and Hardstark try to dispel them by hyping up law enforcement. It’s easy for law enforcement to be romanticized in these discussions, as listeners love stories with a hero or a masterful detective that brings justice to the bad guys. If Kilgariff and Hardstark feed into their (mostly) white female listeners’ paranoia that they will be victims of crime and urge them to call law enforcement anytime their paranoia surfaces, they should also raise conversations about bias-based calls to police and police brutality. Kilgariff and Hardstark Go Overboard With Praise For Private Detectives The fact that Kilgariff and Hardstark promote strong detective work in the cases they cover isn’t necessarily wrong. Unfortunately, sometimes, the pair go overboard with their praise for some private investigators, even making former investigator Paul Holes a celebrity for his work with Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office on the Golden State Killer case. Holes’ work does deserve mention in the case, but so does the fact that the Golden State Killer was also a former police officer. Police Corruption Is Ignored Kilgariff and Hardstark only showcase the positive aspects of law enforcement while shying away from the topic of police corruption. Of course, law enforcement professionals are not always heroes and have often been the criminals in true crime cases (Golden State Killer), as well as inhibitors by refusing to thoroughly investigate cases involving victims who aren’t white and heterosexual. Encouraging The Death Penalty My Favorite Murder has also been accused of being bloodthirsty, with Kilgariff and Hardstark advocating for harsh punishment, including the death penalty. Again, this is a narrow way of viewing criminal justice without accounting for wrongfully accused individuals and racial and economic biases. The Billy Jensen controversy In response to Kilgariff and Hardstark’s insensitivity, and ignorance, fans can use their tired defense that we just “don’t get” My Favorite Murder and its humor. However, it’s difficult to see how they can excuse the allegations regarding Billy Jensen. After My Favorite Murder took off, Kilgariff and Hardstark founded Exactly Right Media in 2018. It is a podcast network with 16 podcasts, including My Favorite Murder and The Murder Squad. The Murder Squad was a podcast by Holes and journalist Billy Jensen. While the podcast was a hit, it was abruptly canceled in 2022. It soon surfaced that the podcast was canceled amid sexual misconduct allegations against Jensen. Podcaster Jenn Tisdale came forward with allegations of assault and harassment against Jensen on her podcast Too Many Jennifers. After she came forward, many other women with similar allegations quickly followed. However, Tisdale’s podcast also revealed some shocking allegations against Exactly Right Media. Tisdale explained that an employee of Exactly Right Media reached out to her and detailed their allegations of sexual harassment against Jensen. A Lawsuit Against Exactly Right Media The employee went to the higher-ups at the company with their allegations but was allegedly told to continue working with Jensen. This even led to the employee filing a lawsuit against Exactly Right Media for ignoring their allegations and forcing them to continue working with Jensen. Tisdale claimed she was called to testify in the case, which ultimately settled in mediation. Are The Allegations Against Exactly Right Murder True? It’s unclear if the allegations against Exactly Right Media are true. However, if they are, it raises scrutiny of Kilgariff and Hardstark. They are the founders of the podcast network that ran The Murder Squad and likely would’ve been among the higher-ups involved in Jensen’s case. Or at least one or both had some level of awareness. While they are not responsible for Jensen’s actions, they certainly are responsible for protecting their employees, which they failed to do most egregiously if Tisdale’s allegations are true. To this day, neither Kilgariff, Hardstark, nor Exactly Right Media have publicly addressed the claims surrounding Jensen. The Takeaway Kilgariff and Hardstark, their podcast, My Favorite Murder, and Exactly Right Media have found themselves in a perfect storm of allegations and fan uproar. Several of the recent revelations against Kilgariff and Hardstark and My Favorite Murder has sullied their reputations. A more important question is, have these allegations sullied the entire True Crime genre or not?

Question: What is the Megan's Law website?

At the federal level, Megan's Law requires persons convicted of sex crimes against children to notify local law enforcement of any change of address or employment after release from custody (prison or psychiatric facility). Megan’s Law website was developed to honor Megan Kanka, a young girl who was m*rdered and to incorporate information regarding Megan’s Law. Megan's Law is the name for a federal law (and an informal name for subsequent state laws) in the United States, requiring law enforcement authorities to make information available to the public regarding registered s*x offenders. The laws were created in response to Megan Kanka’s crime. Federal Megan's Law was enacted as a subsection of the Jacob Wetterline Crimes Against Children and S*xually Violent Offender Registration Act of 1994. This requires sex offenders to register with local law enforcement. Since only a few states required registration before Megan's death, the state-level legislation to bring states in compliance—with both the registration requirement of the Jacob Wetterling Act and community notification required by federal Megan's Law—was crafted simultaneously and is often referred to as "Megan's Laws" of individual states. Thus, the federal Megan's Law refers to community notification (making the registry information public), whereas state-level "Megan's Law" may refer to both s*x offender registration and community notification.

Question: Did director Mike Nichols know actor Dustin Hoffman before he cast him as the lead in the hit movie The Graduate?
Answer: Director Mike Nichols, in the documentary Becoming Mike Nichols, explained that when he was working on the movie, The Graduate, it had a very limited budget. He couldn’t use a major actor. So he started to look for an unknown actor A Graduate Movie Poster He didn’t know Dustin Hoffman, but he had seen him acting in a little play in an off-Broadway where he played a transvestite Russian fish wife. After Nichols and his team had tested “lots of people, hundreds of people” without success for the role of Benjamin Braddock, he remembered seeing Hoffman in the play. He told his team, “I did see a very talented guy. I have no idea if he’s right for this. Let’s get him out here and test him.” Hoffman went out to Hollywood to test for the role of Braddock. Hoffman, Like Elizabeth Taylor, Had A Special & Rare Quality As An Actor Nichols said that Hoffman had a very special and rare quality, just like Elizabeth Taylor had where “there seems to be a deal in the lab where they (the actors) get better in the bath overnight. What you see on the floor when you’re shooting (the movie) is good, but what you see on the screen the next day is quite a lot better.” Nichols referred to the scene where Dustin checks into the hotel to have his first rendezvous with Mrs. Robinson. “Dustin has an astonishing amount of life (when he appears on the film) behind nothing.” He’s not moving anything, he’s not doing anything but you see him in the film (The Graduate), and he’s not doing anything but he’s panicked and I don’t know how we (the audience) know, but we know.” Nichols also explained the trademark whimper Dustin displays when he’s extremely nervous throughout the film, but especially in the hotel room waiting for Mrs. Robinson to appear the very first time. Nichols said he told Dustin how to do that, and it originates from Nichols whimpering every time he had to listen to Jack Warner (Warner Brothers) tell jokes at lunch. Nichols said it was hilarious watching Dustin mimic his own behavior but it really worked for the film. Nichols said that he recruited Sam O’Steen to work on the film as his editor. Sam was Nichol’s handpicked editor who worked with Nichols on Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf and The Graduate. Also, Billy Wilder, who had been “a great pal to Nichols when he was getting ready to shoot Virginia Wolf, lent Nichols his supervising editor. But things didn’t work out, and “the supervising editor” left in three days. Nichols used every trick in his book to make The Graduate a success, including making sure he shot Dustin Hoffman so that he shined in his role. The rest as they say, is history.

Question: Why do so many celebrities have contract riders that no one can look them in the eyes? What’s up with that? Is it an ego thing?
Answer: People who are highly creative, like celebrities, often have odd thoughts and behaviors—and vice versa. Both creativity and eccentricity may result from genetic variations that increase cognitive disinhibition—the brain's failure to filter out extraneous information. Many highly creative people, such as actors, musicians, or other famous people, exhibit personal behavior, sometimes striking others as odd. This is why they have riders added to their contracts and why they insist no one talk to them unless it’s absolutely necessary. Or people can’t look them in the eye. Or whatever they feel protects them and their eccentricity. This is not a new phenomenon. Albert Einstein picked up cigarette butts off the street to get tobacco for his pipe; Howard Hughes spent entire days on a chair in the middle of the supposedly germ-free zone of his Beverly Hills Hotel suite; the composer Robert Schumann believed that his musical compositions were dictated to him by Beethoven and other deceased luminaries from their tombs; and Charles Dickens is said to have fended off imaginary urchins with his umbrella as he walked the streets of London. More recently, we have seen Michael Jackson’s preoccupation with rhinoplasty, Salvador Dal’s affection for dangerous pets, and the Icelandic singer Bjrk dressed for the Oscars as a swan. It isn’t just average Joes who perceive highly creative individuals as eccentric. These individuals often see themselves as different and unable to fit in. The latest findings in brain imaging, creativity research, and molecular biology suggest that these perceptions are not just based on a few anecdotal accounts of “weird” scientists and artists. The Takeaway - Creativity & Eccentricity In fact, creativity and eccentricity often go hand in hand, and researchers now believe that both traits may result from how the brain filters incoming information. Even in the business world, there is a growing appreciation of the link between creative thinking and unconventional behavior, with increased acceptance of the latter. Is it ego? Or just actors and highly creative types who need special protection from their eccentricity? Best wishes to all.

Question: What are the most cleverly designed book covers?
Answer: This Quora question which normally might have piqued my interest, immediately made my stomach ache. Then I would have immediately responded, and it’s all about perspective and personal taste. How Do You Pick Just One? A book cover I think is the most cleverly designed might be considered a dud by others. In 2023 People Judge A Book By Its Cover In current times, most people judge a book by its cover. It’s considered the all-important pictorial introduction to the words within. It’s also considered a crucial element of the reading experience and persuades readers to get past the first page. Some of the most cleverly designed book covers range from iconic to witty to beautiful and thought-provoking. Eat, Pray, Love is considered a classic book, and the cover is considered a fabulous work of book cover art by many. How Hard Can It Be To Write A Book? I spent the past nine months writing and actually completing my first book. My friends and family used to tease, harangue, and bug me, “How hard could it be to write a book?” they would cajole. Yea, sure. It isn’t that hard. Right? Well, speaking from my recent escape from book-writing hell, my answer is an ear-splitting scream followed by a hard “Wrong.” How Hard Is It To Come Up With A Cleverly Designed Book Cover? The book cover design is just one of the many soul-crushing, mind-numbing, heart-stomping decisions you must make to publish your book, even if you only start with an e-book. Unless you happen to be a reincarnated Salvador Dali who can sit down and create an award-winning book cover in your spare time, settling on a cover for your book can be traumatic. Creating Book Covers Can Be Extremely Expensive What many people have never considered is how expensive it is to write and publish a book. Whether you self-publish or get an agent and sell your book to a publishing house. Everything about writing, publishing, and marketing your book - self-published or not - costs money. My first book cover (after multiple debates) for my self-published book. Book Cover Artists I didn’t personally design the book cover for my first book. I hired a book cover artist. She wasn’t cheap, and every revision - big or small - costs money. After the cover artist submitted her designs to me, I socialized with my book editors (I had four different editors, and they all cost money), and they all had different opinions. Wildly different. Some loved it, some hated it, but none of them had to pay the artist. I did. Getting feedback on my book cover was worse than getting a new hairstyle that some people loved and others hated. Once all the opinions - positive and negative were considered - and the cover was finished, there were well-meaning friends who told me how terrible my cover was. Then they told me my book would fail miserably because the cover sucked. I was haunted by the final book cover. I had nightmares. While many people buy books based on their covers, I usually don’t. After going through the entire book cover design exercise, I do pay attention to covers, but I don’t decide whether to buy the book based on the cover. I’m sure many people do. Other Clever Book Covers The most cleverly designed book covers ultimately are a matter of opinion. What one person loves, another one hates. The Takeaway The most cleverly designed book covers ultimately are a matter of opinion. What one person loves, another one hates. Your favorite book cover may or may not be the same as anyone else. Question: Was Eva Longoria's Flamin' Hot Cheetos movie fact, fiction, or both?
Answer: It depends on who you talk to, whether the movie was fact, fiction, or both. The June 13, 2023, Los Angeles Times column by Gustavo Arellano was titled: “Why the Flamin’ Hot Cheetos movie is both pandering and pernicious.” Those were pretty strong “P-words,” but Arellano called it as he saw it. Of course, Eva Longoria was less than thrilled with the article. The movie was her directorial debut, and she was very proud of the film. A scene from “Flamin’ Hot,” a film directed by Eva Longoria about the purported origins of Flamin’ Hot Cheetos. (Searchlight Pictures) The Perfect Journalist To Write The “Flamin’ Hot” Article - Ask A Mexican Gustavo Arellano was the perfect journalist to review the film with a unique perspective on the Mexican American community. Arellano is a highly respected American writer and featured contributor for the Los Angeles Times. He is also the former publisher and editor of Orange County’s alternative paper, OC Weekly. He is also an integral part of the Latino community. Ask A Mexican He is most notably the author of the column jAsk a Mexican! Which is syndicated nationally and has been collected into book form as ¡Ask a Mexican! (Scribner, 2008). Arellano is highly respected as a journalist. Arellano has won numerous awards for the ¡Ask a Mexican! Column, including the 2006 and 2008 Best Non-Political Column in a large-circulation weekly from the Association of Alternative Newsweeklies. He was also awarded the impressive 2007 Presidents Award from the Los Angeles Press Club, an Impacto Award from the National Hispanic Media Coalition, and a 2008 Latino Spirit award from the California Latino Legislative Caucus. The man knows the Latino community and writes from a position of honor and authority. If he describes Longoria’s movie as “pandering and pernicious,” it’s noteworthy. Liar Liar Pants On Fire? Did real-life-janitor-turned-Frito-Lay-executive Richard Montañez really invent Flamin’ Hot Cheetos? Or was he spinning a fairy tale? In 2021 Los Angeles Times writer Sam Dean published an article proving that Montañez was a fibber at best and a fabulist at worst. Hot Cheetos lovers accused the Los Angeles Times of trying to takedown Montañez. But Deam was reporting the facts. Eva Longoria Was Not Happy With The Los Angeles Times Eva Longoria was interviewed by the Los Angeles Times in the spring of 2023 before the movie was released. She dismissed Dean’s reporting by snickering: “[It] feels like L.A. Times would have better resources dedicated to more important things.” For decades, the National Hispanic Media Coalition has righteously called out anti-Latino bias in Hollywood and the national media. They responded to the Montañez criticism from the media by releasing a news release urging people to see “Flamin’ Hot.” L.A. Plaza de Cultura y Artes in downtown Los Angeles hosted a packed outdoor screening earlier in June attended by Longoria, Montañez, and Dolores Huerta (one of the most influential labor activists of the 20th century). The goal was to support Longoria’s film. A Charming Feel-Good Movie Whether It’s A Fairy Tale Or Not I completely believed Dean's findings, but I'm a long-time Eva Longoria fan. I watched "Flamin' Hot." I found it charming and inspirational. Even though I knew about the film’s truth-telling controversy. Besides my appreciation of Longoria, I would have watched the filn just to see Tony Shalhoub (Monk) as Frito-Lay's CEO, Roger Enrico. I also love Dennis Haysber (Clarence C. Baker). He;s also one of my favorites. Should The Facts Be Damned? Yes, I understand the ethical concerns Sam Dean, Gustavo Arellano, and The Los Angeles Times raised. Monica Castillo also raised similar concerns in her June 9, 2023, review of “Flamin’ Hot” for RogerEbertcom. Castillo wrote: “Do we, as a woefully underrepresented group in movies, need this story, facts be damned? As a Latina critic who has been writing about my community’s stories for as long as I’ve had a career, I want better for us and our storytellers. While I enjoy some aspects of this movie, I’m not sure the means justified the lackluster result. Instead, Longoria's film becomes an extended lesson in tying a product to cultural identity, targeting an audience, and how to monetize them as prospective consumers. It’s just business, baby, and sometimes the characters in the middle get lost in the capitalist shuffle. Then again, Montañez’s self-mythologizing is his business, and this movie is now an extension of those efforts to rewrite history—a product placement, if you will—cinematically solidifying his alleged role in a product he didn’t create.” Longoria Is A Staunch Supporter Of The Latina Community Castillo noted: “My ethical qualms aside, Longoria channels the hard-working Mexican American/Latino/immigrant ethos in her film, showing genuine love and respect for the hustle that keeps food on the table and the lights on despite impossible odds,” “What does it say when we lionize a person who says they did something they didn’t and hold them up as a pillar of our community, who, if anything, perfected selling our connections to our culture back to ourselves as a form of identity consumerism?” Indeed, what does it say? All very good points. Artistic License Can Be Fraught With Danger As a writer, I understand the desire to punch up a story to add drama or entertainment. But I also worry about wandering too far from the truth. I recently finished my first true crime book for publication and worried incessantly about getting the facts right. I nagged my editors to avoid introducing any word art that might stretch artistic license. I understand the dilemma Longoria and her writers might have struggled to overcome. Their are many fine lines. The Life Of Richard Montañez Is Inspirational What is true about the film is that Montañez’s life is an inspiration. He really was a high school dropout from Ontario who rose through the ranks of Frito-Lay and now travels the country to speak about his unlikely rise. But as Sam Dean pointed out in his 2021 LA Times article, Montañez didn’t invent Flamin’ Hot Cheetos — others at Frito-Lay did. The film states that Montañez came up with the idea for Hot Cheetos in 1992, even though Dean’s article showed that was the year the snack debuted nationwide after ongoing successful test runs in Texas and the Midwest. Credit should always be given to those who truly deserve it. As Gustavo Arellano summarizes: “The details of history don’t matter to Longoria; Mexican pride does. “Flamin’ Hot” is the type of feel-good treacle that high school teachers screened for their Mexican American students when I was coming of age in the 1990s to make us feel better about ourselves. Teachers today will no doubt do the same for their students. That’s what makes “Flamin Hot” not just pandering but pernicious.” The Takeaway Although I enjoyed the film, I knew before I watched it that Richard Montañez did not personally invent Flamin' Hot Cheetos. I give Longoria kudos for her work and directorial debut, which must be deemed successful on many levels. Not everyone will love the film, but I found it charming. Kudos need to go to Gustavo Arellano, Sam Dean, and Monica Castillo for honoring journalistic integrity and reporting the true facts about Richard Montañez. In the world of 2023, it's comforting to know that there are still writers willing to risk criticism by speaking their truth. Thank you to Arellano, Dean, and Castillo. Should you see the film? It's a good story about a young man who beat the odds to build a great life for his family. Is Eva Longoria's Flamin' Hot Cheetos movie fact, fiction, or both? It’s both. Just remember the story has some elements of fantasy. Then sit back and be entertained.

Question: Is a movie being made about the Game Stop/Reddit battle against Wall Street?
Answer: Yes. Dumb Money First Look: The GameStop Stock Frenzy Is Now a Movie Paul Dano, Seth Rogen, America Ferrera, and Pete Davidson star in the true-life tale of Reddit vs. Wall Street. From a 2023 perspective, the financial war depicted in Dumb Money may seem like a dimly remembered headline from a bygone time. The so-called GaneStop Short sequence squeeze happened in January 2021, when the world was reeling from many far bigger problems: COVID lockdowns, vaccine shortages, and the Capitol insurrection. In the shadow of such colossal events, a disparate group of small-time investors began driving up the stock price of a brick-and-mortar video game store that had previously been destined for oblivion. The fluctuations of a single stock would hardly have garnered much attention—except that this vast group of small-scale investors, unifying mainly in Reddit groups and the comment threads of YouTube videos, managed to line their pockets (at least temporarily) while upending the balance sheets of a small cadre of ultrawealthy, politically connected millionaires and billionaires. Robinhood The GameStop buyers literally used a stock-buying app called Robinhood, which allowed them to take from the rich—like investment management firm Melvin Capital, which had placed large bets that the company would continue to collapse—and give to the poor (namely, themselves). Now their story is being told in the movie Dumb Money, featuring an all-star cast that includes Paul Dano, Seth Rogen, America Ferrera, Pete Davidson, Shailene Woodley, Nick Offerman, Anthony Ramos, and Sebastian Stan. The backstory of how it unfolded is like a cross between Caddyshack and Wall Street, with the nobodies outmaneuvering the somebodies—at least until the rules abruptly change. Rogen, who plays one of the multi-millionaire hedge fund managers whose business goes topsy-turvy because of the GameStop rally, says Dumb Money illustrates how much of the financial system is rigged to benefit those who already dominate it. “It is purposely convoluted—you know what I mean?—in a way that is designed to keep people out of it,” he says. “The price of entry is understanding this completely bizarre system. It's so hard! Could you explain to me, conceptually, what stock shorting is and why that is a thing that exists? I still have a hard time wrapping my head around it. And I think that's the point.” Director Craig Gillespie (I, Tonya, and Cruella) saw the GameStop stock frenzy play out in his own household, telling Vanity Fair that a close family member was one of the millions of small-scale buyers who took part. “My son, who’s 24, was very involved in the whole run and happened to be living at our house at the time,” the filmmaker says. “So through him, I got to experience the emotional roller coaster and the pain and the frustration and the outrage.” The movie, set to debut on September 22, 2023, is based on the nonfiction book The Antisocial Network by Ben Mezrich. The screenplay is by Rebecca Angelo and Lauren Schuker Blum, and both Orange Is the New Black writers who previously worked as journalists. Gillespie added his son’s eyewitness experiences to the mix, although most of the smaller buyers are fictionalized amalgams. “We tried to cover the gamut of the various scenarios that happened,” Gillespie says. “There were the early traders that got in and made money. There were the traders that came in too late. They were the ones that didn’t sell, which sadly was quite a lot of people. So we tried to represent the various groups.”

Question: Has the missing actor Julian Sands been found?
Answer: According to People Magazine “human remains have been found in the area Julian Sands disappeared on California’s Mount Baldy,” authorities have confirmed. "At about 10:00 a.m., civilian hikers contacted the Fontana Sheriff’s Station after they discovered human remains in the Mt. Baldy wilderness," San Fernando Police said in a statement released on Saturday. "Fontana Station deputies, along with the Sheriff’s Department’s Emergency Operations Division, responded to the scene." Mount Baldy. Although police did not mention Sands by name, the remains were discovered in the same area of the Californian mountain that the Oceans Thirteen actor was hiking in when he was reported missing in January. "The decedent was transported to the Coroner’s Office, pending positive identification. Identification should be completed next week," the statement said. Representatives for Sands did not immediately respond to PEOPLE's request for comment. The discovery comes after the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department shared a statement from the Sands family last week, five months after the 65-year-old A Room with a View actor went missing while hiking Southern California's Mount Baldy in January. "We are deeply grateful to the search teams and coordinators who have worked tirelessly to find Julian," they said. "We continue to hold Julian in our hearts with bright memories of him as a wonderful father, husband, explorer, lover of the natural world and the arts, and as an original and collaborative performer." The sheriff's office added in the tweet, "Although missing hiker, Julian Sands, was not located during the recent search mission, the case remains active. We want to thank everyone who assisted in the June 17 search and the previous search missions." Sands was first reported missing in the Baldy Bowl area on Jan. 13, by his wife, Evgenia Citkowitz. Crews continued their search for the Leaving The Las Vegas star over that weekend using helicopters, drones, and infrared devices but were still unable to locate the missing actor, the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department said. Officials had also previously attempted to retrace Sands’ steps and ping his cell phone to locate the English star. In a Twitter post shared by the sheriff's department on Jan. 23, the sheriff's department confirmed that the search for the missing Sands was continuing and added that the department would "continue to utilize the resources" it has at its disposal. Along with the department's update, it shared a statement from The Sands family, who extended their gratitude to the "heroic search teams" who continued to aid in the search for the missing actor. "We are deeply touched by the outpouring of love and support," the statement read. "Our heartfelt thanks to the compassionate members of the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department who are coordinating the search for our beloved Julian." An avid hiker, Sands told The Guardian in 2020 that a "remote peak in the high Himalayas, such as Makalu" topped his bucket list — and that the closest he’d ever come to death was during an excursion in the Andes Mountains in the early 1990s when he and three others were "caught in an atrocious storm above 20,000 feet." "We were all in a very bad way. Some guys close to us perished; we were lucky," he added. Sands also told the outlet that he would like to be remembered "as an interesting, amusing father by my children" — and that the most important life lesson he has learned is "to be nice, and grab [life] with both hands, we know it is short." The actor's brother Nick Sands said in January that he believed Julian, whom he affectionately calls "Jules," was "gone," telling the Craven Herald & Pioneer on Jan. 24, "He has not yet been declared missing, presumed dead, but I know in my heart he’s gone." "However, sibling rivalry being what it is, it would be just like him to walk out of there and prove me wrong," Nick added.

Question: What made Frank Sinatra so obsessed with Ava Gardner?
Answer: Frank Sinatra (December 12, 1915 – May 14, 1998) was a married man the very first moment he set eyes on Ava Gardner. Regardless, he told friends that he was going to marry her. He said she was the prettiest woman he had ever seen. His wife would not be an issue. He assured those who listened. It would all work out the way he wanted it to. Ava Gardner (December 24, 1922 – January 25, 1990) was also married at the time. Ava Gardner and Frank Sinatra - Image from Wikimedia. Ava was no stranger to having affairs. Because of her beauty, celebrity, and the financial success of her movies, many people turned a blind eye to her personal life and scandals. By the age of 23, she had been married twice. The number of affairs she had during her marriages is said to be in the double digits. It was considered shocking for the time. None of that mattered when the two met for the first time. A Secret Affair There was explosive chemistry between them, and those who witnessed it were blown away. The affair began that night. They were careful not to get caught in the first weeks. In 1949, the pair was caught on a date. This time it made headlines across the world. The press had a field day. She was a part of the Golden Age of Hollywood. Two of the biggest stars in Hollywood carrying on an illicit affair was a dream come true for them. It was also a dream come true for Frank. His dream girl was on his arm and madly in love with him. And he felt the same about her. There was nothing that could stop them. Nothing except Frank’s wife, Nancy. She was long-suffering as the wife of a global superstar and a man who did not meet a woman that he didn’t take to bed. His new affair was different from the rest. This affair would end the Sinatra's marriage. They No Longer Hid Their Affair They flaunted their love everywhere they went but particularly when they were in New York City together. Early in their relationship, Louis B. Mayer had enough of Frank and dropped his contract at MGM. Ava, however, was the most popular star on their roster and the actress who made them the most money. Mayer wasn’t the only one fed up with their antics. Nancy Sinatra Filed For Divorce Nancy Sinatra grew tired of being humiliated by the affair. She filed for divorce. As the battle heated up, she asked for custody of their three young children. Frank Was Furious With Nancy’s Request After some back-and-forth negotiations, the Sinatras were able to come to an agreement. Their divorce was finalized. He was lighter in the wallet but free to pursue a stronger commitment with Ava. As she awaited news that Frank was freed from his marriage, Ava got devastating news. A sex worker came forward with a claim that she and Frank had been having an affair. Ava confronted Frank with the allegation. He denied it, but there was a crack in the relationship. Still, a few days after his divorce was done, the pair married. The Pope condemned the pair. Many suspected that once Ava and Frank were married, they would calm down. Those who thought that was wrong. The pair were as determined to give people something to talk about as they ever were. Love And Marriage The fights between the pair were legendary. Insults flew between the two as easily as I love yous. Just when it seemed like they were on the brink of breaking up, the two would reconcile. And just as their arguments played out in public, so did their makeup. Fueling the arguments were insecurities from both of them, each finding a reason to be jealous of someone in the other’s life and Frank’s career being on a downswing. Two Abortions During the course of their marriage, Ava terminated two pregnancies. When confronted by Frank about why she would do that when he wanted a family with her, her answer was devastating. She told him that their relationship was too unstable for her to bring in children. Her greatest desire was to have children but give them a stable environment like she had growing up. Frank lashed out and began sleeping around. He didn’t try to hide the fact that women still found him attractive and even flaunted some of his infidelities for the cameras. The message was sent to Ava that this marriage was over. Her response was to flaunt her affair. She jetted off to Madrid and made headlines for her relationship with Luis Miguel Dominguin. The passion between them was off the charts. A decision was made to end the relationship with Sinatra. She filed for divorce in 1954. Come Fly With Me Frank was not willing to let go of the relationship that easily. He fought to win back Ava’s love. His efforts included public declarations of love and promises of fidelity, and private gestures like sending flowers. But his wife was not having any of it. Still, for three years, Frank did everything he could to win back the affections of the love of his life. There was nothing he wouldn’t do to reconcile with her. For a few weeks, it appeared as though Ava’s relationship with Luis was cooling, and the old spark came back with her husband. That was not the case. Ava was steadfast in her belief that the relationship with Frank, while passionate and full of fun, was not good for her mental health. She wanted a loving relationship with a stable partner. Something that she did not see happening with Ol’ Blue Eyes. In 1957, Frank granted the divorce. Like their relationship, the breakup was front-page news all around the world. The mega stars’ every move was tracked by paparazzi and tabloid reporters. Every salacious secret was craved by the newspaper editors to sell more papers and by the public eager to see that celebrities were just like them. It was very public heartache. The news wasn’t all bad for Frank, though. Because he had lost the girl of his dreams, the public saw him through a different lens. He was one of them. And it propelled his music career to heights that he couldn’t have guessed they would go. The Takeaway Ava Gardner never married after she divorced Frank Sinatra. They remained lifelong friends until her death. Frank Sinatra married Mia Farrow (1966–1968) and then Barbara Marx (1976 - May 14, 1998). He was married to Barbara Marx until his death in 1998. While tragic, the love story of Ava Gardner and Frank Sinatra continues to fascinate people in 2023.

Question: Will a new hair growth formula be derived from hairy moles?
Answer: Amplifica’s Osteopontin is a molecule believed to be the trigger for growing hair in moles. Amplifica has performed research on growing hair in moles. The company’s founder Dr. Plikus and his research team (Maksim Plikus and Natasha Mesinkovska) discovered the molecule that makes hairy moles grow hair. Plikus partnered with the renowned Dr. William Rassman to create Amplifica. Dr. Rassman announced his involvement on Redditt in July 2022. Amplifica just completed a $11.8 million Series A financing round. Research into this molecule has been ongoing for 10 years by an international team of scientists. More importantly, osteopontin can induce hair follicle growth when administered anywhere on the skin. The initial work on osteopontin was performed on mice, but Amplifica has announced that future treatment and trials will likely involve a combination of osteopontin and some other newly-discovered hair-growing proteins, such as SCUBE3. Plikus and his team have also researched SCUBE3. Part of the ongoing research would include trials where osteopontin and the SCUBE3 would be combined into one formula and needled into the scalp of balding men and women to reawaken dormant hair follicles. The procedure would be a near-painless procedure similar to Botox injections. Dr. Plikus was quoted as saying: The new formulation of osteopontin and SCUBE3 when applied to balding scalps: "Will grow (hair) like you remember when you were 18. It would not grow like wiry armpit hair. Instead, the molecule burst is shown to hair follicles on a scalp, and they're like, 'OK.OK, Time to grow." Osteopontin was part of ongoing studies by Follicum, a company that disbanded in 2021 but came back in 2023 under new ownership. Their use of an osteopontin-based peptide slightly differed from what Amplifica will do via osteopontin (plus another molecule) injections. Follicum’s Phase 2 clinical trials resulted in a hair growth increase of 6.6 hairs/cm2, which was deemed insufficient to continue with Phase 3 trials at the time. Hopefully, Amplifica will see more favorable results. Human trials on Amplifica’s lead compound (likely not SCUBE3) are expected to begin later in 2023.
